card.name: Words just before a proper name
card.fires_on: Words that sit just before a capitalised name or title, such as a possessive, an adjective of nationality, or the start of a place name. Seen in historical and place-name text, and after 'Trialists' in a study name.

modes.label: Possessive before a group
modes.description: A possessive pronoun after 'and' that leads into a noun for the person's people or staff.
modes.example: The palace was constructed as a home at Haga for the Queen and<< her>> children, and not as an official residence

modes.label: Start of a place or institution name
modes.description: A word or letter that opens a named place or body, such as 'V' in Vindomora or 'Royal' before Academy.

card.writes: It weakly favours name-like pieces such as Nick and Nic, and suppresses unrelated pieces, so the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It fires on small words that come right before a name or title, like 'Royal' before Academy or 'her' before a person's children.
